title: Tailoring the thermal stability and dielectric response of GO–PVA–AgNW nanocomposites through gamma irradiation
content: The effects of high-dose gamma irradiation on the thermal behavior, water solubility, and dielectric response of GO–PVA–AgNW nanocomposites were investigated. Films prepared by the solution-casting method were irradiated at doses of 250, 500, and 1500 kGy and examined using FTIR, TGA/DTG, DSC, gel-fraction measurements, and dielectric spectroscopy over the frequency range of 120–1 MHz and the temperature range of 293–383 K. The FTIR results revealed dose-dependent changes in the O–H, C–H, and C–O bands, consistent with modifications in the molecular environment and polymer–nanofiller interactions. While the pristine film dissolved in water within approximately 30 min, the irradiated samples exhibited gel fractions of 53%, 66%, and 81%, respectively, supporting the formation of a crosslinked polymer network following irradiation. TGA revealed the highest residual mass in the sample irradiated at 1500 kGy. The degree of crystallinity reached its minimum value of 7.50% at 1500 kGy. Dielectric permittivity and loss tangent generally decreased with increasing frequency and increased with temperature. AC conductivity increased with both frequency and temperature. Irradiation generally reduced the dielectric response and AC conductivity. The obtained results demonstrate that high-dose γ-irradiation is an effective tool for purposefully modifying the thermal stability, water solubility, and dielectric response of GO–PVA–AgNW nanocomposites.
